anatomy.intro: Compare four visible structures; this schematic is not a measurement or identification test.

parts.function: The oval blade forms the broad surface of each leaf.
parts.label: Leaf blade

parts.function: Pink veins branch across the green blade.
parts.label: Netted veins

parts.function: The creeping stem carries leaves and visible hairs.
parts.label: Hairy stem

parts.function: A short stalk joins each blade to the stem.
parts.label: Petiole

flowers.text: Small pale tubular flowers sit among overlapping bracts. Indoor flowering is uncommon.

habitat.text: Kew places Fittonia albivenis in the wet tropics of South America. Nightly is a nursery trade selection; its label does not establish a wild collection locality.

image.alt: Generated Fittonia anatomy schematic: 1 leaf blade, 2 pink netted veins, 3 hairy stem, 4 petiole; educational illustration rather than collection identification evidence.
image.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: square botanical anatomy illustration for a personal gardening field guide. Create a detailed naturalistic watercolor and fine colored-pencil schematic of Fittonia albivenis with pink netted veins, green leaf margins, oval pointed thin leaf blades, short petioles and visibly finely hairy branching creeping stems. Show a small leafy shoot enlarged, isolated on a warm ivory background, no pot, no soil, no roots. Generous clear margins. Exactly four dark-green numbered circles with fine leader lines and small endpoint dots: 1 points to the broad leaf blade away from its veins; 2 points precisely to the pink netted vein network on another leaf; 3 points to fine hairs along a clearly visible stem segment; 4 points precisely to a short petiole between stem and leaf blade. Make all four targets exposed and unambiguous. Numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 are the only text, each appears once. Botanical educational schematic, not a photograph, diagnosis or depiction of a confirmed cultivar. No branding, no watermark, no decorative labels, no invented flowers.

lookalikes.text: Other selections share the species and netted leaf pattern. Color alone cannot independently verify the Nightly trade identity.

mature.text: Proven Winners describes Nightly as a spreading plant about 4–8 inches high. This is a product description, not a measurement of P39.

milestones.text: Purchased at Home Depot in Howell and watered with RO water after extremely dry medium, as clarified by the owner October 22. Plant photographs and a Network News Nightly label were supplied October 21; exact watering time and volume remain unrecorded.
milestones.title: Purchase, RO watering, and label photographs

milestones.text: The owner confirmed quarantine in another room. An irregular glass pot with a drainage hole and exterior-only acrylic paint is planned, with new VERYPLANTS mixes incoming. Dimensions and final mix are pending; no completed repot was reported.
milestones.title: Quarantine and planned repot clarified

nameStory.text: Kew dates the accepted Fittonia albivenis combination to 1979 and its earlier Adelaster name to 1861. These are nomenclatural dates; Nightly’s introduction date remains unverified.
